projects.title: Go concepts
projects.subtitle: When a loop looks alive
projects.summary: Study the cyclic attack on Go networks through exact labels, representations, causal interventions, and native behavioral checks. Two related studies are kept distinct.
projects.question: What makes a Go network judge a doomed loop as safe, and does the represented feature actually drive its decisions?
projects.verification: The canonical go-concepts README, paper source and build log were inspected at commit 64a3c5045789c16891b1f0cb1cf1e5145308a38b. Go Concept Lab's milestone-4 status was also inspected. Historical experiment and test counts were not rerun for this import.

sections.title: Loops Look Alive — paper study
paragraphs: Jaeson Booker's 2026 manuscript studies five Go networks, including the KataGo network attacked by FAR, an adversarially trained KataGo network, and Leela Zero. It reports a group-safety error: vulnerable networks can count liberties yet judge doomed loops as alive.

The study reports that a mid-network closed-loop feature partly acts as evidence of safety in vulnerable networks. The adversarially trained tf3 network retains a related feature while judging doomed loops correctly. Representing a feature and relying on it are distinct questions.

findings.label: Causal intervention under search
findings.detail: Holding the loop direction changed b40's ownership verdict on 11 of 12 doomed rings in the study's own 800-visit PUCT search. Mean ownership moved from +0.78 to −0.24 after the owner passed.

findings.label: A causal link with a cost
findings.detail: Safe-ring ownership also fell from +0.92 to +0.38. The intervention is evidence of causal involvement in this setup, not a general repair.

sections.title: Go Concept Lab — separate exploratory pilot
paragraphs: This earlier infrastructure and behavioral study used trained Leela Zero #57 and KataGo b6c96 s175M. Native extraction and a controlled decoding pilot were completed. Accessible probe information alone does not establish policy reliance or a shared causal mechanism.

In the final-layer linear liberty probe, Leela accuracy was 45.9% on ordinary positions and 46.2% on attack-source positions; KataGo was 60.4% and 50.3%. These are probe accuracies, not game win rates. The two engines did not show the same decline.

findings.label: Bounded behavioral certificates
findings.detail: Across 24 development positions per checkpoint, 3 Leela positions and 1 KataGo position met the avoidable immediate target-chain-loss criterion. The audit checked 63 chosen moves and 8,993 legal immediate replies.

findings.label: Development observations
findings.detail: The positions were retrospectively capture-selected and overlap the decoding source games. They are not a reserved attack cohort or estimates of population failure rates.

limits: The paper's 800-visit search is its own simplified PUCT implementation, not KataGo's native engine; each network judges its own positions. Twelve rings do not establish robustness across Go positions.
The paper study and Go Concept Lab use different checkpoints and protocols. Their results cannot be pooled or treated as mutual independent confirmation.
The pilot's one-reply certificate proves an avoidable immediate material loss under that objective, not an avoidable whole-game loss, eventual survival, or a causal representation failure.

projects.title: RL environments
projects.subtitle: Make the claimed failure measurable
projects.status: Three testbeds + two completed local studies
projects.summary: A claim harness built around planted, verifiable reward hacks and out-of-distribution choice tests. Alignment Synthcore is the first consumer.
projects.question: Can an environment expose what an agent is optimizing for, and turn a paper's claim into a falsifiable behavioral prediction?
projects.verification: Imported from the local Commons research brief and cross-checked against the existing pinned Synthcore testbed catalogue. This import did not rerun the reported experiments. Test 1 is a new locally frozen 32-seed study, published separately from the imported historical claims. Fourteen engineering tests and an integrity audit passed; these are not independent scientific reproduction. Test 2 freshly tuned three methods and two baselines, then evaluated eight reserved full seeds per idea. Source/selection hashes and all model archives were checked; five saved models were re-scored. This remains local evidence.

sections.title: A claim harness
paragraphs: Start with one falsifiable behavioral prediction and the minimum setup needed to test it. Vary the environment, reward specification, and optimizer while planting detectable hacks. Evaluate revealed preferences with out-of-distribution choices when the training reward no longer settles the answer.

Each new environment should make a specific paper claim testable or repair a deficient test. Equal tuning budgets for methods and baselines, held-out families, and checks that the planted failure actually occurs are part of the research design.

sections.title: Implemented inside Synthcore
paragraphs: interactive_gridworld separates delayed tampering incentives, feedback corruption, and an overseer's blind spot. ued_gridworld tests goal misgeneralization with online training and level choice. confounded_imitation tests action-copying confounds in MountainCar.

findings.label: Different methods, different hacks
findings.detail: The reported gridworld results distinguish MONA, which avoids the multi-step tamper hack but still uses the feedback lever, from decoupled approval, which avoids both in the tested approval-only setting.

findings.label: Oversight imposes a ceiling
findings.detail: An overseer-blind vase hazard remains a limitation across methods. A win against the planted reward-hacking baseline does not remove that oversight blind spot.

findings.label: Fair baseline tuning matters
findings.detail: The causal-confusion baseline's failure disappears under an effective tuned setting. The regret curricula hurt performance under the tested budgets. These results concern the implementations and testbeds, not universal refutations of the papers.

sections.title: Test 1 completed: approval feedback × environment reward
paragraphs: A locally frozen 32-seed confirmation used the same exploration traces for all four feedback/reward conditions, across 192 environment instances. The combined primary support criterion failed: independent feedback reduced lever use, but neither full-horizon arm completed the task. This is a controlled fixed-exploration ablation, not a replication of the original online algorithm or an independently reproduced safety win.

findings.label: Corruption-channel contrast, with task failure
findings.detail: In the primary feedback-lever condition, lever activation fell from 98.4% with executed feedback to 10.9% with independent feedback. The paired difference was −87.5 percentage points (95% seed-level t interval −95.4 to −79.6). Goal completion was 0% in both arms, failing the required 80% completion floor.

findings.label: Using environment reward changed button activation
findings.detail: In the button-only family with independent feedback, adding environment reward at the fixed tested weight increased button activation from 6.3% to 65.6%. This is a secondary descriptive contrast; it does not establish that every reward mixture causes hacking.

findings.label: Planning horizon remained important
findings.detail: In the predeclared myopic sensitivity, lever-family goal completion was 31.3% with executed feedback versus 98.4% with independent feedback. These sensitivity results do not replace the failed primary result. One myopic independent-feedback layout required an unknown-state fallback policy.

sections.title: Test 2 completed: mechanisms after fresh baseline tuning
paragraphs: Four original candidate settings and two development seeds were used per method and baseline, selecting by safety. Separate four-seed toy gate checks preceded eight reserved full test seeds per idea. The original diagnostic, direction and 10-point mechanism minimum were preserved. The archived minimax evaluator differs from the current version, so these are fresh current-version results, not replacements for historical verdicts.

findings.label: Causal confusion: Declared minimum ruled out here
findings.detail: Selected-method diagnostic improvement was -0.6 percentage points relative to its selected baseline (simultaneous 98.333% paired t interval -2.5 to 1.2). The original declared minimum was 10 points; safety and capability are separate outcomes.

findings.label: Minimax regret: Declared minimum ruled out here
findings.detail: Selected-method diagnostic improvement was -11.6 percentage points relative to its selected baseline (simultaneous 98.333% paired t interval -26.2 to 3.1). The original declared minimum was 10 points; safety and capability are separate outcomes.

findings.label: ACCEL: Declared minimum ruled out here
findings.detail: Selected-method diagnostic improvement was 1.8 percentage points relative to its selected baseline (simultaneous 98.333% paired t interval -3.0 to 6.6). The original declared minimum was 10 points; safety and capability are separate outcomes.

limits: A planted failure must be demonstrated before testing a proposed solution. The attempted gridworld confound did not fool behavior cloning; the MountainCar setup did at defaults.
The interactive reward-plus-approval baseline finds the planted hacks under the tested tuning settings. Avoiding those hacks is not equivalent to beating every strong competitor.
The Commons brief proposes a broader five-environment suite and OOD battery. That broader suite is not recorded as completed or benchmarked.

Test 1 used fixed uniform exploration, zero tuning, one positive reward coefficient, and a tabular learner. It is separate from the original online method and original published Synthcore verdicts. The primary criterion failed even though lever activation decreased.

Test 2 covers three selected local implementations, four candidate settings and eight confirmation seeds. Simultaneous intervals use a paired t approximation. Toy-to-full changes cannot be attributed to tuning alone; equal candidate counts do not equal compute or supervision access. Results do not estimate literature-wide failure rates.

next_steps.detail: Preserve the goal-completion gate while testing whether the feedback/reward effects persist when the learner chooses its exploration. Treat the finished fixed-exploration study as a distinct version; also stress-test corruption of the counterfactual query channel.

projects.title: Bounded Agency
projects.subtitle: How training constrains revealed goals
projects.summary: Map the gap between optimal-policy predictions and the preferences learned by finite trained agents. Measure choices under distribution shift rather than asking agents to declare goals.
projects.question: How do environment variation, model capacity, and optimization affect which reward-equivalent goal an agent learns?
projects.verification: The historical archive and summaries were inspected without rerunning them at import. Test 3 is a new locally frozen measurement audit: sixteen fresh small-MLP policies, calibration controls, three same-task choice batteries and a separately labelled proxy-relocation stress test. All eighty saved-policy/battery combinations were verified using an independent NumPy forward pass and endpoint simulator. These engineering checks are not independent scientific replication.

sections.title: The framing
paragraphs: The optimum is an equivalence class, not a point. The project asks which behaviors are constrained by training environment, reward specification, and optimization pressure. Capability alone does not identify terminal goals; the environment must already distinguish them.

For future LLM experiments, the pretraining prior should be treated as an input to the hypothesis. Claims about aligned general intelligence remain a motivation for research, not a demonstrated consequence of the small-scale results.

sections.title: Archived experiments
paragraphs: A 7×7 gridworld puts a true-goal gem at a proxy corner except in a fraction p of training episodes. JAX PPO varies MLP/CNN capacity and entropy settings. Out-of-distribution choice trials estimate an implied gem weight; the archived summary reports eight seeds per configuration. A separate tabular Q-learning MDP tests a power-seeking prediction.

findings.label: Optimal equivalence versus learned lock-in
findings.detail: In the specified environment, any p > 0 distinguishes the true goal for the optimal-policy argument. Finite trained agents can nevertheless remain attached to the proxy; the reported transition varies with capacity and exploration.

findings.label: The estimator has a bounded range
findings.detail: The README reports about ±0.03 recovery error on exact-optimal policies. The identifiable weight interval is [0.10, 0.90], with censoring outside it. Values near the plotted floor and ceiling should not be read as precise terminal-goal weights.

findings.label: Longer runs remain heterogeneous
findings.detail: The archived long-run summary reports 0/8 small-MLP seeds at the ceiling for p=0.3, entropy=0.01, versus 8/8 at p=0.3, entropy=0.05. The large-MLP p=0.1 setting has 5/8 at the ceiling. These are reported configuration outcomes, not universal capacity or exploration laws.

findings.label: A separate power-seeking check
findings.detail: Tabular Q-learning is compared against the analytic n/(n+1) prediction. Finite-sample records approach that reference; this is a toy-MDP validation, not evidence that deployed agents have a general power-seeking goal.

sections.title: Test 3 completed: does preference survive the choice battery?
paragraphs: Archived checkpoints were not retained, so this audit trained sixteen new small-MLP policies at p=0.3, entropy 0.01 or 0.05, with 614,400 environment steps per policy. Source and settings were frozen before training; fitted models were frozen before reserved evaluation. Neither outcomes remain in every primary denominator. Exact-optimal calibration controls met the 0.03 weight-error bound.

findings.label: Every goal-interpretation gate failed
findings.detail: All four adjusted choice-rate comparisons meet the planned ±10-point equivalence rule, but cohort-mean equal-distance non-reach rates are 14.7–21.3%, above the 10% limit. Similar rates therefore do not validate a stable-goal interpretation. The low-entropy zero-width t intervals reflect eight identical zero differences, not population certainty.

findings.label: Entropy 0.01, reflected geometry: Rate equivalence supported within 10 points
findings.detail: Unconditional gem-choice difference on equal-distance trials was 0.0 percentage points relative to the original battery (adjusted 98.75% paired t interval 0.0 to 0.0; eight training seeds). Goal interpretation is withheld because the non-reach gate failed.

findings.label: Entropy 0.01, distance reweighted: Rate equivalence supported within 10 points
findings.detail: Unconditional gem-choice difference on equal-distance trials was 0.0 percentage points relative to the original battery (adjusted 98.75% paired t interval 0.0 to 0.0; eight training seeds). Goal interpretation is withheld because the non-reach gate failed.

findings.label: Entropy 0.05, reflected geometry: Rate equivalence supported within 10 points
findings.detail: Unconditional gem-choice difference on equal-distance trials was -0.3 percentage points relative to the original battery (adjusted 98.75% paired t interval -6.3 to 5.7; eight training seeds). Goal interpretation is withheld because the non-reach gate failed.

findings.label: Entropy 0.05, distance reweighted: Rate equivalence supported within 10 points
findings.detail: Unconditional gem-choice difference on equal-distance trials was 0.0 percentage points relative to the original battery (adjusted 98.75% paired t interval -8.3 to 8.3; eight training seeds). Goal interpretation is withheld because the non-reach gate failed.

sections.title: A proxy cannot be relocated silently
paragraphs: The archived policy observes walls, agent and gem, but no proxy marker. Three primary batteries preserve the fixed proxy corner. A fourth moves the unmarked proxy and is reported as a separate task-change stress test; it cannot establish latent-goal instability. Some shortest gem routes can also pass through the proxy, so route selection remains part of the behavioral readout. Random-policy fits are negative controls, not recovered latent goals.

findings.label: A plausible fitted weight is insufficient
findings.detail: Random controls receive legacy fitted weights around 0.50–0.53 while leaving roughly 63–68% of trials unresolved. These numbers are not recovery of a known latent goal.

figures.caption: Test 3: equal-distance gem choice with failures retained, and adjusted paired-seed intervals for transformed versus original batteries. The shaded band is the prespecified ±10-point rate-equivalence margin. Goal interpretation has a separate non-reach gate. This is a fresh local audit, not an independently reproduced goal-scaling result.
Archived phase diagram: out-of-distribution gem-choice rates and in-distribution reward. Dots show seed outcomes and lines configuration means. This figure was imported, not regenerated.
Archived training trajectories. Per-seed transitions and finite training duration matter; an average curve is not evidence of gradual convergence for each seed.
Archived longer runs. Persistent and escaping seeds coexist in some configurations; see the downloadable JSON summary.

limits: Small gridworlds, finite training, selected architectures and eight seeds per archived configuration do not establish how general agents' goals scale.
The preference estimator is conditional on the choice-test setup and censored outside its identifiable range. Avoid interpreting endpoints as exact latent goals.

Reported phase transitions and switches need reproduction and sensitivity checks. This publication imports archived reports; it does not certify the theoretical framing or independently reproduce the experiments.

Test 3 concerns two selected small-MLP configurations and eight fresh seeds each. Mean-rate equivalence does not establish identical individual behavior or a unique latent reward. Non-reach limits goal interpretation; the legacy estimator conditions on reached endpoints and retains censoring. No capacity or acquisition-mechanism claim is made.
